The Senior Total Rewards Operations Manager supports global total rewards programs, working with Payroll, Finance, People Operations, People Technology, Legal, People Business Partners, brokers, and vendors. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

What does software planning look like when people and artificial intelligence agents work together? As a Staff Product Manager for Planning at GitLab, you'll help answer that question and lead the team toward a clear product direction. This isn't just about improving traditional agile planning. You'll rethink how intent becomes actionable work, how that work moves through software development, and where human involvement is needed.

You'll develop a point of view on planning's future and turn it into product decisions with engineering, design, and product leadership. That includes exploring how planning could connect work to business priorities and budgets, rather than assuming the answer is already decided. Alongside that strategic work, you'll share ownership of existing planning capabilities with another product manager.

We're opening this role at Staff level, with flexibility to consider Principal level based on your experience and scope of impact.

What you'll do

  • Define a clear direction for planning as software development shifts toward collaboration between people and artificial intelligence agents, and help the team move from open questions to concrete priorities.
  • Shape how users capture intent, break it into actionable work, and determine which work can proceed autonomously and which needs human involvement.
  • Evaluate whether and how planning should connect software delivery to company priorities, business objectives, and budgets.
  • Share ownership of planning capabilities, including work items, boards, specifications, and portfolio planning, with a fellow product manager. Help define how that scope is divided.
  • Work with engineering and design to translate product direction into a roadmap and improvements to planning workflows across GitLab.
  • Communicate your recommendations clearly to senior leaders, challenge assumptions constructively, and lead the team through changes in direction.

What you'll bring

  • Experience leading product strategy and execution for software development, developer tools, or planning products, with the depth to make decisions in a specialized product area.
  • A strong understanding of software development and development and operations (DevOps) workflows, including how planning decisions affect downstream delivery.
  • The ability to form and defend a product point of view in an uncertain, changing market, while staying open to different ideas.
  • Clear communication with technical teams and senior executives, including experience challenging leadership decisions constructively and building support for a direction.
  • The ability to connect a forward-looking strategy to practical product decisions and work collaboratively across product, engineering, and design.

About the team

The Planning team builds the capabilities at the start of GitLab's software development workflow, including work items, boards, specifications, and portfolio planning. Decisions here affect how work moves through the rest of the platform, so the team's scope extends beyond standalone project management tools.

You'll work alongside another product manager and partner with engineering and design across this product area. The division of product ownership is still being shaped, and you'll help define it. The hiring manager wants you to bring a different perspective, question established approaches, and challenge senior leaders constructively, with room to influence decisions beyond your immediate product scope.

GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our platform brings software development, security, and operations together.

  • Partner with regional sales and engagement leadership to prioritize and manage services opportunities that support critical deals and strategic initiatives, providing clear recommendations on risk management, negotiation strategies, and commercial structures.
  • Foster a culture of enablement and continuous improvement by training field teams on how to position and sell professional services by sharing trends, feedback, and suggestions that improve go-to-market content and operational processes.

What you'll bring

  • Demonstrated progressive experience structuring, scoping, and selling professional services engagements in the region
  • Proven success operating in a pre-sales context, conducting discovery, designing outcome-oriented proposals, and developing custom statements of work (SOWs) and staffing plans for large, complex implementation projects.
  • Solid understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps practices, and cloud transformation initiatives, with the ability to connect technical solutions to mission objectives and measurable business outcomes.

As an Intermediate Fullstack Engineer (Ruby/Vue.js), Growth at GitLab, you'll help turn GitLab's self-serve funnel into a reliable source of new paying customers. You'll work on the in-product journey from a user's first visit through sign-up, trial, and first purchase, on both GitLab.com and self-managed GitLab. You'll collaborate closely with Product Managers, UX Designers, and Data Analysts, with a particular focus on backend development in Ruby on Rails and frontend work in Vue.js. This role gives you the opportunity to combine your fullstack engineering skills with product thinking and experimentation, shipping small changes quickly and measuring their impact on real customer outcomes.

  • Making it easier for self-managed users to try and buy GitLab
  • Building upgrade prompts where users run into paid features
  • Improving the trial experience, including trials of GitLab Duo

What you'll do

  • Maintain and improve our experimentation framework and tooling to increase experiment throughput and reduce the time from setup to results.
  • Collaborate with other Engineering teams, including Fulfillment, to remove purchase barriers across GitLab’s codebase.
  • Document decisions, review code, and share experiment results asynchronously so distributed teammates can track shipped changes and their measured outcomes.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Professional experience developing with Ruby on Rails and modern JavaScript, along with solid Git, feature development, and deployment workflows.
  • Experience working with relational databases and a solid understanding of web performance optimization.
  • A track record of shipping features to production and owning them after release.
  • Ability to use product data to decide what to build, keep, or roll back.
  • Ability to document decisions and share updates asynchronously with distributed Product Management, UX, and Data teammates.
  • Ability to organize your work, seek and apply feedback, and collaborate inclusively with teammates from diverse backgrounds, in line with GitLab’s values.
  • Preferred, not required: experience with Vue.js, PostgreSQL, A/B testing, feature flags, experimentation frameworks, or SaaS sign-up, trial, billing, or checkout flows. We'll help you learn our tooling.

We’re GitLab’s Growth team: one team with one roadmap, prioritizing work by how directly it helps people buy. We work fully remotely and asynchronously across multiple regions, guided by GitLab’s values of transparency and iteration. Our challenge is running more high-impact experiments, faster, while coordinating changes with teams like Fulfillment and Pricing across the parts of the product they own. For more on how we work, see the Growth and Product sections of the GitLab handbook.

About the role
We're looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Repository Services team in GitLab's Create stage. The team owns the repository side of Source Code: how code gets into a repository, who may change it, and how those changes are verified. We build this as an access layer on the primitives the Gitaly team provides, for GitLab's own features and for the artificial intelligence agents now writing and pushing code alongside people.
You'll work in one of GitLab's oldest and most complex product areas, using Ruby and GraphQL across GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated. Repository Services is a new team, and its first months are about reliability and support, so you'll spend real time on performance and structured query language tuning, caching, rate limiting, testing, observability, and resiliency, with experienced team members to lean on. You'll collaborate with product management, product design, testing, security, user experience research, technical writing, Gitaly, Code Review, and the other Source Code teams.

What you'll do
  • Develop secure, well-tested, performant features and improvements using Ruby and GraphQL.
  • Work through complex requirements and legacy constraints to deliver clear solutions while protecting the reliability of this critical system.
  • Design and maintain backend services, application programming interfaces, data models, and business logic that control how code reaches a repository, who may change it, and how it is verified.
  • Build on the primitives Gitaly provides and work closely with the Gitaly team.
  • Triage and fix bugs and support requests for the features the team owns.
  • Collaborate across functions and teams, both asynchronously and synchronously, and involve domain experts when their input will improve the outcome.
  • Use artificial intelligence agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output.
  • Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews.
  • Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency.
  • Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
  • Professional experience building backend web applications, services, or application programming interfaces, with experience using Ruby and GraphQL.
  • An understanding of relational databases, structured query language, data modeling, caching, background processing, and backend performance practices.
  • Experience contributing to user-facing workflows and maintaining their underlying systems.
  • Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes.
  • Experience using artificial intelligence coding agents and reviewing their output, or an interest in building these skills in a complex monorepo.
  • Clear written and spoken English communication skills, including sharing useful status updates in a remote, asynchronous environment.
  • The ability to manage assigned priorities, work through ambiguity, take ownership of your work, and seek guidance when needed.

About the team
Repository Services is a small backend team in the Create stage, formed in September 2026 when Source Code split into focused teams. As the split is finalized we expect to own repository mirroring, Git Large File Storage (LFS), protected branches and Branch Rules, push rules, Code Owners (shared with Code Review), and commit and tag signing. We build on Gitaly's primitives and meet regularly with the Gitaly team, and our work serves GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated.

An overview of this role

As a Senior Compensation Manager at GitLab, you'll lead the design, planning, and execution of compensation programs that help us attract, retain, and reward team members. You'll own recurring programs, including the annual focal merit cycle, and provide guidance and oversight for promotion cycles, quarterly equity grant cycles, and semi-annual bonus programs. Working closely with Total Rewards leadership and partners across People, Finance, and Legal, you'll turn program objectives into clear deliverables, establish processes and controls, and see complex cycles through from planning to closeout. Your work will help ensure accurate, timely delivery and a clear experience for leaders, People teams, and team members.

You'll be based in the United States. We prefer a West Coast location to support collaboration with stakeholders across time zones.

What you’ll do

  • Lead compensation programs from design and readiness through approvals, processing, communication, and post-cycle review, including ownership of the annual focal merit cycle and oversight of promotion, quarterly equity, and semi-annual bonus cycles.
  • Define program calendars, decision points, responsibilities, controls, and success measures. Coordinate dependencies and keep stakeholders informed of progress, risks, and decisions.
  • Ensure compliance with eligibility rules and develop process documentation, manager resources, and communications. Advise People Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, and leaders on program application and exceptions, escalating policy and governance decisions when needed.
  • Analyze compensation data and program outcomes, develop recommendations for Total Rewards leadership, and partner with Finance on budgeting, cost modeling, and reconciliation.
  • Partner with People Technology and IT systems stakeholders to improve workflows, reporting, and usability.
  • Validate inputs and outputs, ensure timely processing, maintain audit and control documentation, and protect confidential compensation information.
  • Oversee the annual refresh of global compensation and equity ranges to ensure accuracy, and support compensation partners with program delivery and analysis.
  • Lead improvements that reduce program risks and friction, strengthen consistency and transparency, and improve the team member experience. Use clear documentation and asynchronous communication to coordinate work across time zones.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience designing and operating compensation programs, with expertise in corporate compensation and public company equity and a record of delivering complex merit, equity, bonus, or promotion cycles accurately from planning through closeout.
  • Strong analytical and spreadsheet skills, including interpreting compensation data, building scenarios, checking assumptions, and explaining findings to decision-makers.
  • An understanding of compensation governance, data integrity, and controls, with discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential information and sensitive decisions.
  • The ability to translate policy and strategy into operating procedures, system requirements, and stakeholder guidance, plus experience with human resources information systems and compensation planning tools such as Pave and Workday, and comfort working on a Mac.
  • Attention to detail, practical problem-solving skills, and the persistence to work through complex issues and deliver accurate outcomes. You can learn unfamiliar programs, systems, and business contexts quickly.
  • The ability to build trusted partnerships, advise leaders and People teams, resolve ambiguity, and move decisions forward without relying on formal authority.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to coordinate with global partners across time zones using asynchronous practices.
  • Helpful, but not required: experience supporting a global, distributed workforce, including partners in India or other locations outside the United States; compensation-cycle communications; and experience in a software or technology company.

The current Compensation team consists of 2 Global Compensation Partners and a Lead Total Rewards Program Manager that collaborates with the Compensation and Benefits teams. An overview of this role

As a Staff Product Manager on the Tenant Scale area within Infrastructure Platforms, you’ll set product direction for how GitLab supports large, complex customers as they grow across departments, projects, and regions. This role focuses on the product choices needed to make tenant data more portable, scalable, and ready for a unified deployment model across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and, over time, Self-Managed. You’ll work on problems that sit at the intersection of product strategy, infrastructure, and customer needs, including how we build a platform to horizontally scale our SaaS architecture, how to enable tenant movement between environments, how isolation and regional requirements are handled, and what needs to be in place to support a more cellular architecture.

At the Staff level, your scope extends beyond a single group. Your direction will inform the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction, you’ll make the investment case for unified deployment capabilities, and you’ll be a recognized authority, inside and outside GitLab, on multi-tenant and cellular SaaS architecture. In your first year, you’ll partner closely with engineering and product peers to define requirements, drive alignment, and move this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on, while coaching fellow product managers as they pick up work from the shared pool.

What you’ll do

  • Drive product strategy and direction for tenant scale and unified deployment capabilities across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and future deployment models, informing the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction and moving this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on in your first year.
  • Set quarterly and annual plans for tenant portability and platform unification, breaking large epics into issues and minimal valuable changes (MVCs) and practicing iteration across multiple groups.
  • Define requirements for our unified deployment platform, including the capabilities needed before tenants can be hosted in a unified deployment unit.
  • Partner closely with engineering counterparts and highly technical teams to turn infrastructure constraints and platform needs into clear product direction.

  • Translate complex technical concepts into product plans, priorities, and documentation that align distributed teams on delivery milestones for tenant portability and platform unification, using error budgets and other performance indicators to inform direction.
  • Represent GitLab as a trusted voice on cellular architecture and tenant scale in customer calls, events, and other external forums.
  • Coach fellow product managers on direction updates, customer validation, and GitLab’s architecture and tech stack, and support a collaborative team model where product managers share ownership across a common pool of work and step into the areas where they can have the most impact.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience managing product work in technical domains such as infrastructure, scalability, platform architecture, software delivery, or cloud services, with results delivered across a range of product areas rather than a single one.
  • Ability to work effectively with deeply technical engineering teams and build credibility in discussions about system design, deployment models, and platform constraints.
  • Knowledge of how SaaS or platform-based systems scale, including concepts such as multitenancy, horizontal scalability, autoscaling, workload isolation, and production readiness, and the ability to build a deep understanding of GitLab’s architecture and tech stack and coach others on it.
  • Comfort working with customers or internal stakeholders on complex requirements, including operational, compliance, or regional deployment needs.
  • Skill in turning ambiguous technical problems into clear product strategy, quarterly and annual plans, priorities, and actionable work.
  • Expertise in qualitative customer interviewing and product validation, with the ability to teach those techniques to others.
  • Experience building business cases, including weighing build, buy, and partner options and forecasting benefits against the competitive landscape.
  • Experience collaborating across product, engineering, user experience, and other cross-functional partners in a distributed environment, using iteration and influence to raise the performance of peers beyond your own group.

  • Recognition as a thought leader in a relevant domain, internally and externally, for example through speaking, writing, or representing your company at customer events and conferences.

The team sits within Infrastructure Platforms and works on foundational platform capabilities.   • Provide temporary coverage for other executive support partners and lead special projects and ad hoc requests across the CRO organization.

  • Clear, approachable communication across functions and levels, sound judgment with confidential information, and the ability to build trusted working relationships.
  • Practical experience using AI tools to improve administrative work, with the judgment to validate outputs, capture context, and retain responsibility for the result.
  • An organized, reliable approach to balancing priorities across two leaders and their teams. We welcome transferable skills from different executive support backgrounds; prior go-to-market experience isn't required.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Regional Marketing Manager, you will own regional marketing for the sales team in your territory and set the standard for how the regional team plans and runs its work. You will choose, plan, and run the events and campaigns that create, expand, and accelerate pipeline in your region, and you will move easily between high-level strategy and creative, detailed execution. Staff is a leadership-level individual contributor role: you lead through the work you build and ship, not through direct reports. In a modern marketing organization, that means building and running your own plans, programs, measurement, and AI-assisted automation instead of handing them off, and it suits builders who are comfortable being a leader without a team to manage. Your audience is CIOs, CTOs, VPs of engineering and platform, and the security leaders who govern how their teams ship software. You will judge audience quality by seniority and buying role, not headcount, so you will need to understand how they work and what they want from a vendor.

You will support both direct and channel sales teams, work with GitLab partners on Channel and Alliance Marketing activities, and partner with external agencies and third parties to prepare and run campaigns. As a senior individual contributor, you will mentor other regional marketers, help build and improve team process, and share best practices with regional peers by planning and operating transparently. Your impact is measured in pipeline: the target is 10X spend contribution to sales pipeline for your region, with your regional budget spent within 5% variance. This role supports one of our sales regions (AMER, EMEA, or APAC), and involves travel up to 50% of the time.

What You’ll Do  

  • Drive results for your region as its marketing leader: own the pipeline and growth outcomes, and go beyond events and experiences to bring partners in to drive marketing across channels, in support of growth through our revenue team.
  • Adapt digital and content marketing programs to the needs of your regional sales team.
  • Create, expand, and accelerate sales opportunities through regional and account-focused campaigns that promote GitLab’s products and services, within the marketing strategy.
  • Set regional event and campaign strategy, with discretion over which events and campaigns best support regional sales goals, and manage events onsite, including logistics, booth staffing, and swag.
  • Project manage every campaign from start to finish, following the GitLab process, so each one meets its objectives, arrives on time, and stays within budget, then measure and report on its effectiveness.
  • Lead cross-functional work to drive demand generation and regional marketing plans, and advocate for your sales region within marketing and for marketing with your sales team.
  • Support Channel and Alliance Marketing activities with GitLab partners, from campaign approval through execution.
  • Work with external agencies and third parties to prepare, manage, and execute campaigns.
  • Mentor and guide regional marketing specialists and managers, and lead in building and driving process within the team.

What You’ll Bring 

  • Proven ability to build and execute  a regional strategy, with a record of delivering, accelerating, and expanding sales pipeline through regional marketing.
  • Experience supporting both direct sales and channel sales teams, and in enterprise solution demand creation and regional marketing.
  • Exemplary analytical skills and a proven aptitude for using data to optimize program performance and inform future strategies.
  • Excellent communication skills, with a proven ability to convey ideas and data clearly in writing and in presentations to a variety of audiences, without a fear of over-communicating. You plan and operate transparently and share best practices with other regional marketers.
  • A proven aptitude for building and driving a budget within your territory, and extreme attention to program details and deadlines.
  • The capacity to empathize with CIOs, CTOs, VPs of engineering and platform, and the security leaders who govern how their teams ship software, and a passion for, and substantial understanding of, the developer tools, IT operations tools, and/or IT security markets.
  • Ability to use GitLab, and you share our values and work in accordance with them.
  • Ability to travel up to 50% and to comply with the company’s travel policy.

Regional Marketing at GitLab turns marketing strategy into regional action. We support our sales teams in AMER, EMEA, and APAC by running the events and campaigns that build pipeline in their territories, working with direct sellers, channel sellers, and alliance partners. We work closely with Product Marketing, Corporate Events, Digital Marketing, Marketing Operations, Developer Relations, Business Development, Customer Success Managers, and Solution Architects. Our goals are set through the Marketing OKRs and measured in pipeline contribution and regional budget. As a Senior Professional Services Engineer at GitLab, you'll work directly with customers to deliver installation, migration, training, and advisory services that help them adopt GitLab successfully. You'll lead engagements from single-node Omnibus installs to large reference architectures built with infrastructure as code (IaC) and configuration as code. You'll also guide migrations from other systems to GitLab SaaS or self-managed deployments, and help customers make practical decisions that improve reliability, security, and day-to-day workflows.

In this role, you'll work closely with customers and GitLab's product and engineering teams to drive customer success and share feedback that improves GitLab and how we deliver services. You'll manage multiple projects at once, mentor other Professional Services Engineers, and help streamline how we deliver consistent outcomes in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.

Some examples of our projects:

  • Designing and delivering GitLab installations and reference architectures using tools like Terraform and Ansible across major cloud providers
  • Leading migrations to GitLab SaaS or self-managed GitLab, and turning customer feedback into actionable improvements for GitLab's product and engineering teams

What you’ll do

  • Deliver GitLab Professional Services engagements, including installation, migration, training, and advisory services across GitLab capabilities.
  • Plan and execute deployments ranging from single-node Omnibus installations to large reference architectures using Infrastructure as Code and Configuration as Code practices.
  • Lead migrations from multiple source systems to GitLab SaaS or self-managed GitLab, helping customers adopt secure, reliable workflows.
  • Partner with Engagement Managers and Project Managers to improve delivery consistency, remove friction, and continuously refine delivery processes.
  • Serve as a trusted technical advisor for customers, translating goals and constraints into practical implementation plans and clear next steps.
  • Interface with GitLab's product and engineering teams to unblock customer outcomes and share feedback that helps improve GitLab features and services.
  • Mentor Associate and Intermediate Professional Services Engineers, providing technical guidance, helping remove blockers, and supporting increased autonomy.
  • Manage and deliver multiple customer engagements at once, either as the primary engineer or as a lead providing oversight and direction to other engineers.

What you’ll bring

  • Professional exposure with one or more infrastructure as code or configuration as code technologies such as Terraform, Ansible, Packer, Puppet, or Chef.
  • Professional exposure with two or more cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Microsoft Azure.

This role has a location requirement - Charlotte, NC or nearby.

  • Experience using, deploying, or configuring GitLab, including a solid understanding of Git and source control workflows.
  • Experience delivering customer-facing services such as installation, migration, training, and advisory engagements across GitLab's feature set.
  • Proven ability to independently manage one or more projects and to lead and provide direction to other Professional Services Engineers on complex engagements.
  • Strong communication skills in English, written and verbal, with the ability to provide clear status updates and build consensus with peers and customers in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to take a solution-oriented approach by identifying root causes, proposing options and tradeoffs, and driving issues to resolution while balancing multiple customer engagements in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fully remote organization by communicating clearly in writing, documenting decisions, collaborating asynchronously across time zones, and working in ways consistent with GitLab's values.

We partner closely with Engagement Managers and Project Managers to deliver consistent outcomes, and we work with GitLab's product and engineering teams to share customer feedback and improve GitLab. An overview of this role

As Engineering Manager, Architecture Engineering: Async, you'll lead a distributed group of Site Reliability Engineers and Backend Engineers. You'll support their development and balance production reliability with platform projects, including zero-downtime Redis upgrades, support for single-tenant and cell-based deployments, and the move from queue-based job orchestration to a durable workflow engine.

What you'll do

  • Lead, hire, and grow a team of site reliability engineers and backend engineers, supporting career development, promotions, and onboarding.
  • Own reliability for the job processing and caching platforms, including service-level objectives, error budgets, alerting, and weekly operational reviews.
  • Manage capacity planning, support escalations, and incident follow-ups, balancing operational work with roadmap projects and rescoping work when deadlines can't be met.
  • Run the team's part of GitLab.com's first-tier on-call rotation, including shift coverage, onboarding, and handovers, and serve as incident commander for high-severity incidents.
  • Drive zero-downtime Redis version upgrades and automate operating system patching and reboots.
  • Adapt job processing to run in single-tenant and cell-based deployments.
  • Own the migration from queue-based job orchestration to a durable workflow engine, defining the first use cases, a measurable migration path, and the roadmap.
  • Own quarterly planning and the team roadmap, and clarify shared operational responsibilities with partner teams, including Git storage.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Experience managing an engineering team delivering high-performance services at scale, ideally site reliability engineers or infrastructure engineers running production software as a service systems.
  • Technical depth in background job processing and caching technologies such as Redis and Sidekiq, sufficient to guide decisions about upgrades, capacity, and failure modes.
  • Experience managing reliability against service-level objectives, including defining service-level indicators, setting up burn-rate alerting, and planning capacity.
  • Experience running a 24/7 on-call rotation and coordinating high-severity incidents.
  • A track record of balancing operational work and incident follow-ups with roadmap projects, and pushing back on scope when deadlines can't be met.
  • Experience leading a fully remote team across time zones in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific.

About the team

The Async team runs GitLab.com's background processing layer, from the Sidekiq infrastructure to the shared code that enqueues jobs. Product teams build the jobs; we keep the platform that runs them fast and reliable. Our Redis clusters support caching, sessions, rate limiting, queues, and shared state. We also support data durability through backup and restore verification, object storage, and operational support for Git repository storage. That work includes restore drills, capacity rebalancing, and provisioning. We staff GitLab.com's first-tier production on-call rotation in 8-hour shifts across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific, triaging every paging alert and bringing in the right team when needed.

An Overview of this role

As a Data Scientist at GitLab on the Enterprise Analytics team,  you’ll be a trusted analytical partner to Sales, Revenue Operations, and Finance, helping define how we measure go-to-market performance and where we invest to grow. This is a strategic and hands-on role. You’ll apply statistical, experimentation, and machine learning methods to forecast outcomes, explain what drives activation, conversion, expansion, and retention, and size opportunities. You’ll also support the company-level reporting and GTM performance views that executives use to run the business, covering consumption, ARR, and first orders.

What you’ll do

  • Embed yourself with business teams to become a trusted partner supporting insight generation and strategic decision making across GTM.
  • Perform exploratory data analysis to uncover behavioral trends, long-term patterns, and the key drivers and levers behind business performance, and communicate their impact clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Build and productionize machine learning models - such as propensity, product-qualified lead (PQL) scoring, churn, and expansion models - including training, validation, testing, and feature engineering, using MLOps practices and tooling (CI/CD for ML pipelines, model registries, automated retraining, and monitoring) to move work reliably from notebook to production
  • Design, run, and evaluate growth experiments (A/B tests and quasi-experiments) on onboarding, pricing and packaging, and upgrade flows, and measure their impact on activation, conversion, and retention
  • Build and operationalize agentic workflows for analysis, modeling, and pipeline automation, with evaluation and monitoring that keep agent-generated insights accurate, traceable, and trustworthy.
  • Contribute to GitLab’s Semantic Layer enabling stakeholders and agents to self-serve metrics using trusts and tested sources.
  • Write production-grade Python and SQL that meets internal standards for style, maintainability, and performance in a high-scale database environment; maintain and advocate for these standards through code review

What you’ll bring

  • 3-5 years of professional experience in GTM analytics, data science, or a similar technical role
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear, measurable questions and communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience with experimentation and causal inference (A/B testing, power analysis, quasi-experimental methods) and with statistical and machine learning methods such as regression, classification, clustering, and survival analysis
  • Deep, hands-on understanding of SQL in cloud data warehouses (like Snowflake SQL), including working with product usage and event data, and in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Hex, or similar)
  • Experience using Python for statistical modeling, machine learning, and production data science. With hands-on experience in pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Jupyter, and related libraries such as LightGBM and XGBoost
  • Hands-on experience building agentic workflows with AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, OpenCode, or similar), including connecting agents to the right context, tools, and platforms such as MLflow, and evaluating their output for accuracy and reliability.
  • Experience working in a B2C company working with motions and metrics, including Consumption, CRR, ARR, and Churn & Contraction
  • Self-motivated and self-managing, with strong organizational skills
  • Ability to use GitLab and to thrive in a fully remote organization

About the Team

The Enterprise Analytics team builds the trusted data products and insights behind GitLab’s Company wide sales, revenue, and finance reporting. We work across the business on metrics including First Orders, pipeline, CRR, ARR, and other key indicators, helping leaders make informed decisions and teams understand how their work contributes to GitLab’s growth.

  1. Drive product impact now. Set the analytical agenda for your product areas and make sure the team's work changes decisions.
  2. Build the merged Data Science function. Define excellence for a Data Scientist who blends analytics and data science, and grow the team to that bar.

You lead mainly through others, and step in hands-on when it matters: reviewing a model, pressure-testing an analysis, or writing the query yourself.

What you’ll do

  • Set a long-range vision and roadmap for Product Data Science, and show the team how its goals connect to company strategy
  • Own prioritization and trade-offs across product areas, and adapt the team as priorities shift
  • Be the go-to partner for Product and Engineering leaders on complex and urgent questions, choosing the right approach: a deep dive, an experiment, or a production model
  • Raise risks and resource gaps early, and bring senior leaders clear options to drive timely decisions
  • Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team: build career paths, act on team feedback, and make tough talent decisions when needed
  • Build a high-trust culture of urgency and accountability, where the team communicates openly, shares progress on a predictable cadence, and delivers quality results on time
  • Set standards for experimentation, causal inference, metric definition, and production modeling

What you’ll bring

  • 10+ years in data science, product analytics, or a related field, including 3+ years managing data science or analytics teams in B2B SaaS or tech
  • Strong product sense and a track record as a trusted partner to Product and Engineering leaders
  • Exceptional communicator who makes complex problems and findings clear to any audience, from Product leaders to executives, and coaches others to do the same
  • Thrives in ambiguity: structures undefined problems, gathers the right information, and makes sound decisions on high-risk, cross-team issues
  • Courage to challenge: offers dissenting views, asks tough questions, and fosters inclusive debate
  • Deep expertise in statistics and experimentation, including hands-on use of quasi-experimental methods (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, propensity score matching)
  • Expert SQL (Snowflake preferred) and strong Python, with experience taking ML models to production
  • Fluent with AI tools, with sound judgment on when AI output can be trusted
  • Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values

Nice to Have

  • Experience with developer tools, DevSecOps, or product-led growth products
  • Experience measuring adoption and quality of AI-powered product features
  • Thought leadership in data science or analytics, internally and externally
  • Advanced degree in a quantitative field

About the Team

Product Data Science brings Data Science and Analytics together into one function. Our Data Scientists are business partners first, pairing strong product judgment with deep skill in SQL, Python, statistics, and machine learning. We help Product and Engineering decide what to build, measure what worked, and understand how customers get value from GitLab.

The opportunity is growing fast. AI is driving growth in GitLab's consumption business, creating new ways for data to drive growth. As AI takes over routine reporting, the team focuses on the hard problems: experimentation, causal inference, production models, and recommendations leaders act on.

About the role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer, you will take backend features and improvements from clarifying the problem through shipping them and following up in production. You will work within a product area, partnering with Product Management, Frontend, Infrastructure, and Security to deliver predictably and contribute to the quality, security, performance, and maintainability of shared backend code and services. You will be trusted to work with minimal guidance, to know when to seek help, and to communicate clearly in a remote, asynchronous environment — with other tenured engineers alongside you to review your work, think through hard problems with you, and help you grow.

Why you’ll love this role

  • Ownership: You'll take features from requirements through delivery and follow-up; your code will run on a platform used by millions of users.
  • Learning and Growth : You’ll work alongside your engineering team, who treat code review and design review as a learning loop rather than a gate — one of the fastest ways to grow your engineering judgment.
  • Innovative Culture: You’ll use AI as a genuine part of daily engineering work, developing the judgment to know when to trust it and when not to.
  • Autonomy: You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.
  • User-Centric Collaboration: You’ll partner closely with PMs and designers to shape requirements, so you understand why you’re building something, not just what.

What you’ll do

  • Own and Ship Features: Design, implement, test, and ship backend features and improvements with minimal guidance, working in Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern languages.
  • Build for Production: Write maintainable, secure, observable, and performant code. Design and maintain APIs, background jobs, integrations, and bounded service functionality, and work with data models, migrations, indexes, and query behavior.
  • Test and Review: Add and improve automated coverage — unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end where appropriate — and review others’ code for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and operational risk.
  • Operate What You Build: Investigate build, test, deployment, and runtime failures at the feature boundary, identify technical debt and propose practical improvements, and take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
  • Leverage AI: Use AI productively in daily work, validate what it produces, and understand where its limitations matter.
  • On Call Support: Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

  • Backend Fundamentals: Professional experience building and shipping production backend applications, with strong programming, API, database, testing, debugging, and performance fundamentals.
  • Adaptability: Experience with Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern backend language. We value the ability to learn and adapt over mastery of a single language.
  • Feature Ownership: The ability to take a feature from clarification through delivery and follow-up, working independently while seeking input at the right time.
  • Practical Judgment: Sound instincts about security, reliability, performance, maintainability, and operational risk, plus an understanding of modular backend boundaries and the consequences of coupling.
  • Clear Communication: Strong written communication and effective collaboration in a remote, asynchronous environment.
  • AI Fluency: Practical experience with AI coding tools, including the ability to review and correct what they generate.

Helpful experience

  • Production Go services, APIs, concurrency, profiling, or gRPC.
  • Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, CI/CD, or cloud deployment.
  • Rust, particularly for systems, security, performance, or platform work.
  • PostgreSQL, schema evolution, caching, queues, messaging, or event-driven workflows.
  • Observability using metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerts.
  • Contributing to a modular monolith, bounded context, shared component, or independently operated service.

An overview of this role

Support Engineering at GitLab believes that healthy teams deliver a healthy customer experience, and that command during a crisis shouldn't fall to whoever happens to be senior and available. GitLab's global Incident & Escalation Management (IM/EM) function coordinates critical incidents, complex multi-team engagements, and executive-level escalations for enterprise customers. As Escalation Manager, you'll own complex, executive, and commercial escalations where customer trust and the relationship are at stake, alongside or independently of a technical issue.

In this functional role, you'll advocate for customers inside GitLab, coordinate teams toward resolution, and lead relationship repair after the event.

What you'll do

  • Own complex, executive, and commercial escalations end-to-end, as defined in GitLab's IM/EM engagement model.
  • Advocate for customers internally and coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales toward resolution, tracking commitments and holding owning teams accountable to agreed dates and deliverables.
  • Maintain a written, customer-facing resolution plan from engagement through confirmed resolution, updating it at each communication milestone.
  • Coordinate with Incident Managers during concurrent technical incidents to maintain a single, coherent narrative for the customer.
  • Own external escalation communications using GitLab's approved templates and cadence, and represent GitLab in high-stakes customer conversations where clarity and ownership influence retention.
  • Engage Sales, Customer Success, and executive stakeholders as needed, including executive-to-executive communication for Severity 1 and 2 events. Brief GitLab leadership with concise summaries that distinguish what's known, what's unknown, and next steps.
  • Lead post-escalation reviews and relationship repair plans, contribute corrective actions with named owners and due dates to postmortems, and hand the relationship back to the account's Customer Success Manager at resolution.
  • Partner with the Head of IM/EM to develop playbooks, communication templates, and process improvements based on patterns from escalations.

What you'll bring

  • Experience in enterprise technical support, customer success, or incident and escalation management at a business-to-business software-as-a-service or enterprise software company.
  • A track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder escalations end-to-end, including executive customer engagements and structured resolution or account plans.
  • Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical detail into plain-language updates for customers and GitLab leadership.
  • The ability to coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales under pressure without formal authority over those teams.
  • Calm, structured decision-making with incomplete information and the ability to provide a steadying presence in high-stress customer situations.
  • Proficiency with support and coordination tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, Slack, and PagerDuty, or equivalent platforms.
  • Availability for on-call coverage supporting executive escalations as part of a globally distributed team.

  • Nice to have:  Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation or equivalent certification; customer-facing experience with GitLab, development, security, and operations (DevSecOps), continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or cloud-native products; experience with formal escalation or incident command frameworks; or AI-assisted support tools for triage, sentiment analysis, or resolution drafting.

About the team

The Incident & Escalation Management function sits within Support Engineering in GitLab's Enterprise Technology & AI (ETA) division. We operate a follow-the-sun model anchored in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia-Pacific, providing year-round, 24-hour coverage for enterprise customers. Our Escalation Managers work globally rather than within a single region, partnering with Incident Managers, Communications Leads, and regional Support Engineering leadership. You'll help shape our playbooks, templates, and standards as we scale.

An overview of this role

As a Principal Executive Recruiter at GitLab, you’ll lead VP-level and other senior leadership searches across Sales, People, Legal, Finance, and other corporate teams. You’ll partner directly with senior executives to identify, engage, assess, and hire leaders, bringing market intelligence and a research-driven approach to complex, often confidential searches. Alongside owning searches end to end, you’ll help shape the strategies, frameworks, and practices that strengthen executive recruiting at GitLab, balancing search rigor with the agility of a fast-moving technology organization.

What you’ll do

  • Lead VP-level and other senior leadership searches end to end, from search strategy and market mapping through assessment, selection, and closing.
  • Advise C-suite executives and senior business leaders on hiring decisions, challenge assumptions, and navigate complex stakeholder dynamics.
  • Develop talent strategies using market mapping, competitive intelligence, creative sourcing, and recruiting data to guide each search.
  • Build relationships with passive executive talent, understand their motivations, and connect opportunities to GitLab’s mission and business priorities.
  • Partner with hiring leaders to define success profiles, assess executive capabilities and business impact, and guide evidence-based hiring decisions.
  • Own executive candidate relationships and deliver a high-touch experience through compensation discussions, competing opportunities, and negotiations.
  • Manage multiple confidential, business-critical searches with discretion, balancing urgency, quality, stakeholder alignment, and candidate experience.
  • Collaborate with Talent Acquisition leadership and executive recruiting peers to improve search frameworks, assessment practices, reporting, and tools.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience independently leading VP-level and senior executive searches through successful hires in an executive search firm, an in-house executive recruiting function, or both.
  • Executive recruiting experience across functions such as Sales, People, Legal, Finance, or other corporate teams, with the business acumen and curiosity to learn new domains.
  • The ability to build trusted relationships with C-suite executives, influence senior stakeholders, and provide candid, evidence-based guidance on hiring decisions.
  • Skills in talent research, market mapping, creative sourcing, leadership assessment, and engaging and closing passive executive talent.
  • Business judgment, communication, and negotiation skills to navigate sensitive searches, complex compensation discussions, and competing executive priorities.
  • Experience developing or improving executive search methodologies, frameworks, and processes while maintaining speed and flexibility.
  • A hands-on approach to managing multiple high-priority searches independently and working through ambiguity.
  • Experience in high-growth technology or enterprise software organizations, global executive searches, and distributed organizations is helpful.

About the team

You’ll join a globally distributed, remote-first Talent Acquisition team where clear communication and reliable follow-through matter. Guided by GitLab’s operating principles, including Speed with Quality, Ownership Mindset, and Customer Outcomes, we take ownership, move with urgency and rigor, and focus on hiring outcomes that matter to our internal customers. We share learnings and create reusable resources to continually improve the quality and consistency of hiring across Business teams.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. An overview of this role

Support Engineering at GitLab believes that healthy teams deliver a healthy customer experience, and that command during a crisis shouldn't fall to whoever happens to be senior and available. GitLab's global Incident & Escalation Management (IM/EM) function coordinates critical incidents, complex multi-team engagements, and executive-level escalations for enterprise customers. As Escalation Manager, you'll own complex, executive, and commercial escalations where customer trust and the relationship are at stake, alongside or independently of a technical issue.

In this functional role, you'll advocate for customers inside GitLab, coordinate teams toward resolution, and lead relationship repair after the event.

What you'll do

  • Own complex, executive, and commercial escalations end-to-end, as defined in GitLab's IM/EM engagement model.
  • Advocate for customers internally and coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales toward resolution, tracking commitments and holding owning teams accountable to agreed dates and deliverables.
  • Maintain a written, customer-facing resolution plan from engagement through confirmed resolution, updating it at each communication milestone.
  • Coordinate with Incident Managers during concurrent technical incidents to maintain a single, coherent narrative for the customer.
  • Own external escalation communications using GitLab's approved templates and cadence, and represent GitLab in high-stakes customer conversations where clarity and ownership influence retention.
  • Engage Sales, Customer Success, and executive stakeholders as needed, including executive-to-executive communication for Severity 1 and 2 events. Brief GitLab leadership with concise summaries that distinguish what's known, what's unknown, and next steps.
  • Lead post-escalation reviews and relationship repair plans, contribute corrective actions with named owners and due dates to postmortems, and hand the relationship back to the account's Customer Success Manager at resolution.
  • Partner with the Head of IM/EM to develop playbooks, communication templates, and process improvements based on patterns from escalations.

What you'll bring

  • Experience in enterprise technical support, customer success, or incident and escalation management at a business-to-business software-as-a-service or enterprise software company.
  • A track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder escalations end-to-end, including executive customer engagements and structured resolution or account plans.
  • Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical detail into plain-language updates for customers and GitLab leadership.
  • The ability to coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales under pressure without formal authority over those teams.
  • Calm, structured decision-making with incomplete information and the ability to provide a steadying presence in high-stress customer situations.
  • Proficiency with support and coordination tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, Slack, and PagerDuty, or equivalent platforms.
  • Availability for on-call coverage supporting executive escalations as part of a globally distributed team.

  • Nice to have:  Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation or equivalent certification; customer-facing experience with GitLab, development, security, and operations (DevSecOps), continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or cloud-native products; experience with formal escalation or incident command frameworks; or AI-assisted support tools for triage, sentiment analysis, or resolution drafting.

About the team

The Incident & Escalation Management function sits within Support Engineering in GitLab's Enterprise Technology & AI (ETA) division. We operate a follow-the-sun model anchored in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia-Pacific, providing year-round, 24-hour coverage for enterprise customers. Our Escalation Managers work globally rather than within a single region, partnering with Incident Managers, Communications Leads, and regional Support Engineering leadership. You'll help shape our playbooks, templates, and standards as we scale.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role

As a Data Engineer at GitLab, you'll build, run, and maintain the pipelines and infrastructure that bring data from our enterprise applications, internal systems, and GitLab's software as a service (SaaS) platform into our data platform. Your work will power company reporting, data science, and artificial intelligence (AI) self-service.

You'll own features end to end, from source integration to tested, monitored, documented data ready for use. You'll focus on keeping the platform reliable, secure, and cost-efficient as data volumes and AI usage grow, and making governed data ready for AI tools, agents, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based access. This is an AI-first role: you'll use AI coding agents every day while maintaining high standards for code review and testing. You'll report to the Director, Data Platform.

What you’ll do

  • Build, extend, and maintain extract, load, transform (ELT) pipelines from enterprise applications such as Salesforce, Zuora, Zendesk, and Marketo, internal systems, and the GitLab SaaS platform. Integrate data through application programming interfaces (APIs) and event sources such as Snowplow.
  • Manage and maintain the infrastructure behind the platform, including SaaS tools such as Snowflake, Fivetran, and Monte Carlo, and self-managed services such as Airflow and Kubernetes.
  • Write maintainable, well-tested, performant Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) code that meets our internal standards, and review GitLab team members' merge requests.
  • Own day-to-day platform operations: triage and resolve failed pipelines, infrastructure issues, and GitLab team member requests. Use monitoring, service-level agreements (SLAs), data contracts, query and warehouse tuning, and data quality checks to keep the platform reliable and cost-efficient.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineers, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Data Governance, and business partners so data lands in the shape they need for downstream use.
  • Use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, OpenCode, GitLab Duo, or similar tools to speed up development, debugging, testing, and documentation without compromising review rigor.
  • Apply role-based access control (RBAC) and masking policies to make governed data available to AI tools and agents. Handle data subject to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls, material nonpublic information (MNPI), and personal data safely.
  • Ship medium-sized features independently in small, iterative merge requests, and document architecture and runbooks in the handbook.

What You'll Bring

  • Professional experience shipping production data pipelines in Python.
  • Deep, hands-on SQL skills and experience with a cloud data warehouse; Snowflake is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with ELT or extract, transform, load (ETL) pipelines at scale, including incremental loads, schema changes, backfills, and API ingestion.
  • Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow, familiarity with dbt, and solid data modeling fundamentals, including Kimball dimensional modeling.
  • Experience running and troubleshooting data infrastructure, with comfort using Git-based workflows, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and code review.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding tools in your daily work, with an understanding of where they help and where they fall short.
  • Clear written communication, the ability to use GitLab, and comfort working asynchronously in a fully remote organization in line with GitLab's values.
  • Preferred, not required: experience with Snowflake; Docker, Kubernetes, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Terraform; SaaS application APIs such as Salesforce, Zuora, or Zendesk; data observability tooling; or Snowflake administration.

About the team

The Data Platform team within Enterprise Data is responsible for a scalable, reliable and secure data platform for data analytics at GitLab. That includes managing and maintaining the infrastructure we use, both SaaS and self-managed, and building and maintaining the data pipelines that bring data into it. We make data reliable, secure and ready for analytics, data science and AI tools. As more questions go straight to AI tools and agents, the platform underneath has to be more reliable, better governed and more cost-efficient than ever. We're fully remote and globally distributed, and work asynchronously through issues, merge requests and the handbook.

About the Team

GitLab's APJ Ecosystem team builds and scales the partner (channel, alliance, and hyperscaler) motion across the region. India is a strategic market for GitLab, and this hire is central to strengthening our partner ecosystem there — deepening a smaller number of high-value partnerships rather than spreading thin across many transactional ones.

About the Role

The Scale Ecosystem Sales Manager (ESM), India is a senior, market-facing role responsible for building and scaling GitLab's partner business in India across the full breadth of the ecosystem. This role focuses on new logo acquisition and aligns closely with our new business team in India. This will involve working with  hyperscalers, India-centric system integrators (SIs), and born-in-the-cloud / AI-native partners. We are looking for someone with the range and seniority to credibly own strategic partner relationships across all of these partner types, and to help grow our business through these partners.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who has already built a career scaling partner-sourced and influenced revenue in India — someone who knows the hyperscaler ecosystem (AWS & GCP), has deep, credible relationships with India's major SIs, and understands how to engage newer-generation cloud-native and AI partners as they become an increasingly important part of the go-to-market.

What You'll Do

  • Build and scale GitLab's partner-sourced and influence business in India across hyperscalers, large India-centric SIs, and born-in-the-cloud/AI partners.
  • Develop deep, strategic (not transactional) relationships with a focused set of priority partners — joint business plans, QBRs, and named executive sponsorship.
  • Own hyperscaler relationship management and Marketplace motion with AWS and/OR GCP.
  • Build and grow relationships with major India SIs and market-making channel/born-in-the-cloud partners and emerging AI-native partners.
  • Drive partner-sourced pipeline and bookings, and carry a quota tied to partner-sourced/generated revenue.
  • Partner closely with the India sales team to ensure partner-sourced opportunities are properly identified, supported, and closed.
  • Work with the India and APJ Ecosystem team to help shape and refine the India Ecosystem coverage model.
  • Contribute to partner enablement, certification, and go-to-market programs suited to the India market.
  • Report on partner engagement health, pipeline contribution, and progress against strategic-partner milestones.

What We're Looking For

  • 15+ years of experience in channel/alliance/partner management or ecosystem sales, ideally within enterprise software, DevOps, or cloud infrastructure.
  • Extensive, well-rounded experience scaling a business through partners across hyperscalers, large India-centric SIs, and born-in-the-cloud/AI-native partners — not narrowly specialized in just one partner type.
  • Direct experience managing hyperscaler relationships (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure) including Marketplace motion.
  • A strong, credible existing network among India's major SIs and cloud-native/channel partners, with a track record of moving relationships from transactional to strategic.
  • Comfort carrying a partner-sourced revenue quota and being measured on pipeline origination, not just deal closure.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills — able to align internal sales, marketing, and partner-side stakeholders around joint goals.
  • Native or business-fluent Hindi and strong business English (for regional collaboration with APJ leadership).
  • Based in or willing to relocate to Mumbai OR Delhi.

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience at or with a hyperscaler (AWS, GCP) in a partner or alliances capacity.
  • Familiarity with GitLab, DevSecOps, or adjacent developer-tooling ecosystems.
  • Experience helping design or reset a partner coverage model, comfortable building process rather than only inheriting one.

What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months)

  • Joint business plans and an active engagement cadence (e.g., QBRs) in place across priority hyperscaler, SI, and cloud-native/AI partners.
  • Demonstrable movement of key partner relationships from transactional to strategic engagement.
  • Growing partner-sourced pipeline and bookings against quota.

An overview of this role

As a Journey Architect on GitLab's Digital Customer Outcomes team, you'll design journeys that turn meaningful customer actions into retention, consumption and revenue outcomes. You'll own journey design and service blueprints for assigned customer cohorts, products or coverage models, leading cross-functional work from design through launch. Digital Orchestration builds and runs the journeys day to day; you'll remain accountable for their outcomes and ongoing improvement. You'll add design capacity to help priority journeys, including artificial intelligence (AI) and consumption journeys, launch in fiscal year 2028 (FY28).

What you’ll do

  • Design journeys backward from business outcomes to meaningful customer actions, audiences and engagement tactics. Map each cohort's intended path, timing, signals that customers need help and interventions to get them back on track.
  • Decide which steps are self-serve, AI-assisted or human-led, and define the handoffs between them. Design across in-product guidance, email, events and community, choosing the right channel for each moment.
  • Build service blueprints with Customer Experience (CX) Operations, documenting the people, systems, data, content and handoffs behind each touchpoint. Give every step a trigger, a response, an owner and a metric.
  • Write journey specifications covering steps, triggers, audiences, channels, content, handoffs and metrics. Set build plans, coordinate partner teams and clear dependencies to launch on time and to specification.

An overview of the role 

GitLab is seeking an experienced Principal Security GRC Manager, Legal Assurance to tackle complex customer security challenges at the intersection of technical architecture and business requirements. In this role, you'll apply deep security expertise to answer technical questions, assess contract requirements, and enable GitLab’s Sales and field organizations to address security problems for enterprise customers. You'll work directly with customers and internal teams to provide technical guidance, create security content, and help customers understand how GitLab's security controls meet their compliance and risk management needs.

What you'll do:

Contract & Legal Review

  • Perform comprehensive contract reviews for both customer agreements and vendor relationships
  • Analyze security and compliance clauses in legal documents
  • Provide risk-based recommendations and remediation guidance for contractual security requirements
  • Partner with Legal, Sales, Product, and Procurement teams to negotiate security-related contract terms. Manage escalations, collaborate across other teams, and develop solutions to enable team and business partners to close deals
  • Document and track contract-related security obligations

Customer Engagement & Assurance

  • Join customer and prospect meetings to provide expert guidance on GitLab’s security practices and controls in order to address security, privacy, and compliance requirements
  • Build and maintain templates, playbooks, fallback positions, and training that simplify and accelerate negotiations
  • Facilitate customer assurance activities through our Customer Assurance Activities Service Desk
  • Provide escalation support for complex security questionnaires, RFPs, and risk assessments
  • Serve as security point of contact for enterprise customer questions, requests, and concerns

Security Evangelism & Thought Leadership

  • Act as a trusted technical thought leader, developing internal and external security content such as blog posts, whitepapers, technical standards, and field sales enablement training materials
  • Keep abreast of the rapidly evolving regulatory landscape affecting our agreements. Identify, track, and facilitate solutions for security related customer trends and improvement areas
  • Build and strengthen GitLab's security brand within the industry

Strategic Initiatives

  • Maintain and enhance GitLab's Trust Center and self-service security resources
  • Provide strategic recommendations based on customer security concerns in support of revenue growth
  • Participate in Quarterly Business Reviews to inform product and security roadmap decisions
  • Mentor and provide guidance to Security Assurance team members
  • Drive continuous improvement of Field Security processes and documentation
  • Design and implement solutions to enable Sales facing teams to successfully discuss security problems and topics with customers

What you'll bring:

  • 10+ years of experience in information security, with at least 5 years in customer-facing security roles
  • Deep expertise in security frameworks and standards such as (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/42001, FedRAMP, NIST CSF, etc.)
  • Expertise in law and regulation such as (GDPR, CCPA, DORA, EU AI Act)
  • Proven track record of contract negotiation and security/privacy agreement reviews
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with ability to translate complex technical concepts for diverse audiences
  • Experience creating security content (blogs, whitepapers, presentations)
  • Strong understanding of cloud security, SaaS security models, and DevSecOps practices
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Sales, Legal, Product, and Engineering teams
  • Ability to balance security risk with business objectives
  • Experience speaking at conferences is a plus
  • Preferred: One or more relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CCSP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, or CIPP/CIPM. Equivalent demonstrated experience is equally valued.

Due to government requirements, you must be a United States Citizen (defined as any individual who is a citizen of the United States by law, birth, or naturalization) to fill this position.

About the team

The Security Assurance organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk. Security Governance sits within it and owns customer trust, security awareness, policies and standards, and other governance functions. Our counterparts are Security Compliance, Security Risk, and GRC Engineering.

You will join a small team of four direct reports under the Director, where each person has broad scope and visible impact. We work remote-first and asynchronously, and we write things down and share them openly.

  • Working knowledge of common fraud and abuse patterns, such as account takeover, free-tier and trial abuse, payment fraud and card testing, bot signups, and spam and phishing.
  • Technical fluency with web applications, APIs, identity and authentication, and billing or subscription systems, enough to discuss implementation tradeoffs with engineers.
  • Clear, concise written communication suited to an all-remote, asynchronous environment.

An overview of this role

As a Lead/Principal Journey Architect on GitLab's Digital Customer Outcomes team, you'll connect programs into customer journeys that drive meaningful actions, retention, consumption and revenue outcomes. You'll own journey design and service blueprints, starting with priority cohorts and expanding across products, personas and named, pooled and digital coverage models. Reporting to the Vice President, Digital Customer Outcomes, you'll join as an individual contributor at L5 (Lead/Staff) or L6 (Principal), depending on your experience and scope. At L5, you'll lead journey design and builds for priority cohorts; at L6, you'll own the journey framework across all products, personas and coverage models with division-wide influence. Digital Orchestration builds and runs journeys day to day; you'll remain accountable for their outcomes and improvement.

What you’ll do

  • Design journeys backward from business outcomes to meaningful customer actions, audiences and engagement tactics. Map each cohort's intended path, timing, signals that customers need help and interventions to get them back on track.
  • Decide which steps are self-serve, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted or human-led, and define the handoffs between them. Design across in-product guidance, email, events and community, choosing the right channel for each moment.
  • Build service blueprints with Customer Experience (CX) Operations, documenting the people, systems, data, content and handoffs behind each touchpoint. Launch every journey with a documented blueprint, owners and metrics from the measurement framework, giving every step a trigger, a response, an owner and a metric.
  • Write journey specifications covering steps, triggers, audiences, channels, content, handoffs and metrics. Set build plans, coordinate partner teams and clear dependencies to launch on time and to specification.
  • Specify the content and self-service resources each step needs, and work with content teams to create and govern them. Partner with Lifecycle Marketing on audience, sequencing and delivery so customers experience one coordinated journey.
  • Hand live journeys to Digital Orchestration to run, remain accountable for their outcomes and build in regular optimization cycles with the Digital Outcomes team's Data/Insights partner. Serve as the directly responsible individual for the under-$10,000 digital journey in fiscal year 2028 (FY28).
  • Measure live, measured journey coverage across products, personas and coverage models, step conversion, lift against a holdout or comparison group, meaningful actions, recovery after interventions, time to value and influence on revenue and customer retention. Track partner adoption of the shared journeys and blueprints.
  • Lead journey design and cross-functional builds for priority cohorts at L5; at L6, act as GitLab's single owner of journey design and maintain one consistent framework across products, personas and coverage models.

What you’ll bring

  • Senior experience in customer journey design, service design or digital customer success.
  • A track record of turning journey designs into launched programs with measurable adoption, retention or expansion outcomes.
  • Hands-on experience building service blueprints and designing handoffs between digital and human teams.
  • Working knowledge of journey orchestration, in-app guidance and marketing automation platforms.
  • Comfort defining customer signals, triggers and success metrics, interpreting funnel conversion and running tests.
  • A track record of leading complex, cross-functional builds through launch without direct authority, including planning, managing dependencies and coordinating stakeholders across many teams.
  • Experience in business-to-business software as a service is helpful, as is domain knowledge of development and operations (DevOps) or development, security and operations (DevSecOps).
